settings.heading:
Dogs don't tell you the bed has stopped working.
They show you.
settings.note: Ageing isn't something a bed can undo. What a bed can change is how much work it takes to lie down – and to get back up again.

settings.title: They circle for a long time before they settle.
settings.text: Circling is normal. Circling, re-circling and still shifting ten minutes later usually isn't. It means no position on that bed takes the pressure off.

settings.title: They've started sleeping on the hard floor instead.
settings.text: A dog choosing cold tiles over their own bed is telling you something. Once foam has bottomed out, the floor is genuinely the firmer, more supportive option.

settings.title: Getting up takes a beat longer than it used to.
settings.text: The pause before the first step. The slower rise in the morning. It arrives so gradually that most owners only really notice it looking back.

settings.eyebrow: Two versions of the next six months
settings.heading:
Doing nothing is also a decision.
It just doesn't feel like one.
settings.maths_caption: That's what a £169 bed comes to across the five years its foam core is guaranteed for. He sleeps twelve to fourteen hours a day. There is no other thing you buy him that he will use for that long.

settings.text: He carries on shifting. At nine. At half eleven. At two. You stopped consciously hearing it a while ago – you still wake up.
The fibre keeps packing down exactly where his weight goes: hips, shoulders, elbows. Four small contact points doing all the work.
You buy another bed that looked substantial in the photograph and held its shape for about a fortnight.
He goes back to the rug by the radiator, or your sofa – and you've spent the money for nothing.
One continuous 50kg/m³ core, cut to size. It takes his weight on night one and it is still holding it in year four.
The circle stops after one turn instead of five. He drops his chin onto the bolster rather than the floor.
You notice it first as an absence – the sound of a big dog rearranging himself in the dark simply isn't there any more.
If he doesn't settle on it, we arrange the collection and refund every penny. You don't repackage it and you don't pay for the return.

settings.eyebrow: Why it costs what it costs
settings.heading: Density isn't firmness. It's how much foam is actually in the foam.
settings.body:
Most dog beds are filled with shredded offcuts or low-density foam. They feel wonderful in the shop, and they bottom out inside a year – at which point your dog is sleeping on the floor with a cover over it.

Every PawLunova memory foam core is 50kg/m³. That number is what decides whether a bed is still doing its job in year five. It's also why we're willing to guarantee the foam for five of them.
